posts.topic: Perplexity vs Gemini Deep Research — not interchangeable
posts.hookHeadline:
You're using the
wrong research tool
for the job
posts.hookSub: Perplexity and Gemini are not the same.
posts.hookTTS: You're treating Perplexity and Gemini Deep Research like they're the same tool. They're not. And that's why your research takes twice as long.
posts.agitateBridge: One gives depth — but only if you ask right
posts.agitateTTS: Perplexity is a citation machine. Gemini goes narrative. Use the wrong one for the wrong job — and you rewrite everything.

points.label: USE PERPLEXITY
bullets: Set Focus to Academic mode
Prompt: 'Give me 5 stats with sources on [topic]'
Returns in under 60 seconds
Numbered citations, every claim clickable
points.tts: Perplexity with Academic Focus mode. Prompt: give me five stats with sources. Sixty seconds, peer-reviewed only. No blog noise.

points.label: USE GEMINI
points.verdict: Narrative depth for complex or policy topics
bullets: Use Deep Research mode (takes 5–10 min)
Prompt: 'Deep research: explain [topic] landscape for a non-expert'
Cross-references dozens of sources
Returns a structured report, not a list
points.tts: Last step — and this is the one most people skip. For policy, strategy, or anything narrative — switch to Gemini Deep Research. It takes five minutes. It cross-references dozens of sources. The output is a full report.

posts.proofContext:
Perplexity for data.
Gemini for depth.
Stop rewriting the same research twice.
posts.proofTTS: I haven't fact-checked a stat in weeks. Perplexity cites everything. Gemini explains everything. Two tools, one job each. That's the whole system.
posts.ctaTTS: Save this before you forget it. I drop one of these every day.
posts.ctaSaveText: Save this before you forget it.

posts.topic: More AI use doesn't automatically mean more productivity
posts.hookHeadline:
More AI tools
doesn't mean
you're more productive
posts.hookSub: HBR published the research. It's uncomfortable.
posts.hookTTS: You're adding more AI tools and expecting more output.
posts.agitateMain: AI generates volume. Not always value.
posts.agitateBridge: Polished output isn't the same as good output
posts.agitateTTS: HBR named it workslop — AI-polished content that looks professional but offloads thinking onto your reader.

points.label: THE FINDING
points.verdict: AI intensifies work — it doesn't reduce it
bullets: Berkeley research found AI intensifies work without reducing it
No consistent productivity gains across studies
The variable: how you deploy, not which tool
Judgment-heavy tasks see the biggest losses
points.quickWin: → Source: HBR 2024, Berkeley productivity research (study conducted April-December 2024)
points.tts: Berkeley research found no consistent productivity gains. The variable isn't the tool — it's how you deploy it.

points.label: THE FIX
points.verdict: Use AI for generation, human judgment for decisions
bullets: AI drafts, you decide
Never let AI make the judgment call
One rule: if it requires your expertise, keep it
Automate repetition. Not thinking.
points.tts: Last step — and this is the uncomfortable rule. Use AI to generate, never to decide. Automate repetition. Keep the judgment calls.

posts.proofStat: More AI ≠ more output. Deployment is the variable.
posts.proofContext:
HBR researchers named it workslop.
AI-polished output that offloads thinking onto your reader.
More tools, more workslop — unless you keep judgment in-house.
posts.proofTTS: HBR named the failure mode: workslop. AI-polished content that offloads the thinking. Keep judgment calls human. Generation is AI's job.

posts.topic: Claude Extended Thinking — when to use it and when it wastes your time
posts.hookHeadline:
Claude's Extended
Thinking is costing
you time
posts.hookTTS: Claude's Extended Thinking saves you an hour or wastes twenty minutes. Depends entirely on when you activate it.
posts.agitateMain: Extended Thinking on drafts = slow for no reason
posts.agitateBridge: It only pays off on multi-step reasoning
posts.agitateTTS: Extended Thinking adds depth on complex problems.

points.label: TURN IT OFF
points.verdict: Drafts, captions, rewrites — off by default
bullets: Writing tasks: off
Summarization: off
Translation or reformatting: off
Anything under 2 steps: off
points.quickWin: → Model selector (top of chat) → Extended thinking toggle
points.tts: Turn it off for writing tasks, summaries, captions, rewrites — anything one or two steps. Toggle off in the model selector. Same output, thirty seconds.

points.label: TURN IT ON
bullets: Business strategy decisions: on
Debugging complex code: on
Multi-step planning: on
Anything requiring reasoning chains: on
points.quickWin: → Pays off on problems with >3 steps
points.tts: Strategy decisions, debugging, multi-step planning — turn it on. Problems with more than three steps see real quality gains. Two rules.

posts.proofStat: Extended thinking on for strategy. Off for everything else.
posts.proofContext:
Extended Thinking: on for strategy.
Off for everything else.
Same quality on simple tasks — no waiting.
posts.proofTTS: Complex strategy with Extended Thinking on: deeper reasoning, worth the wait. Simple caption: same output, minutes wasted.

posts.topic: Beehiiv: deleting inactive subscribers improves your newsletter metrics
posts.hookTTS: The counterintuitive newsletter move: delete your inactive subscribers. Open rate goes up. Deliverability improves. Ad revenue follows.
posts.agitateBridge: Low open rates = spam folder = real readers miss you
posts.agitateTTS: Every inactive subscriber drags your open rate down. Low open rates signal spam to providers.

points.label: STEP 01
points.verdict: Set automation to flag 90-day inactive subscribers
bullets: Go to Automations in Beehiiv dashboard
Use the 'Re-engagement automation flow (90-day inactivity)' template from Quick start templates
Review the list monthly
Export before deleting — keep the data
points.tts: In Beehiiv Automations, create a rule: if inactive for ninety days, tag as inactive. Review monthly. Export a backup before you delete anything.

points.label: STEP 02
bullets: Filter by inactive tag
Select all
Delete — not unsubscribe, delete
Open rate climbs as inactive weight lifts
points.quickWin: → Deliverability improves as inactive weight clears
points.tts: Filter by inactive tag, select all, delete. Not unsubscribe — delete. Open rate climbs as dead weight clears. Smaller list, better numbers.

posts.proofStat: Fewer subscribers. Better deliverability. Higher open rate.
posts.proofContext:
Inactive subscribers drag open rate down.
Low open rates signal spam to email providers.
Delete the dead weight — your real readers start seeing you again.
posts.proofTTS: List hygiene is the most underrated deliverability lever. Inactive subscribers hurt you. Delete them.
